extracted.intended_audience: NIH/NIAMS grant applicants (PD/PI), institutional Authorized Organization Representatives (AORs), and institutional officials involved in appeals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how applicants may formally appeal referral/peer-review decisions for NIAMS/NIH grant applications, including required content, allowable grounds, timing, routing, and outcomes. Applies to appeals after study section review and to pre-review assignment disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of appeals — procedural aspects only (scientific opinion excluded)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH has a formal process to resolve disagreements concerning the referral (assignment) and review of applications. Although procedural aspects of technical merit review are subject to appeal, differences in scientific opinion, such as may occur between applicants and reviewers, may not be contested through the NIH appeals process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals based solely on differences of scientific opinion will not be accepted. Formal appeals must be based on one or more specified process-related issues (see allowed bases). Applicants are encouraged to discuss reviewer differences with the program director (often preferred first step).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-appeal consultation with NIAMS program director
rubrics_metrics.description: Before beginning the appeals process, the applicant is strongly advised to speak with the NIAMS program director responsible for the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program director can explain options and consequences and often helps applicants understand the study section's recommendation; in most cases issues can be resolved at this stage and do not require a formal appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal letter — required eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal is a written communication from a PD/PI and/or applicant institution that meets the following four criteria: (1) is received after issuance of the summary statement and up to 30 calendar days after the second level of peer review, (2) describes a flaw or perceived flaw in the review process for a particular application, (3) displays concurrence from the AOR and (4) is based on one or more of the specified issues related to the process of the initial peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An appeal letter that does not meet these criteria and/or does not include the concurrence of the AOR will not be considered an appeal letter but rather a grievance, and will not necessarily be taken to Council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing constraints for appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals must be received after issuance of the Summary Statement and up to 30 calendar days after the second level of peer review. Appeals are due 3 weeks before the applicable Council meeting. An appeal letter will not be accepted before the Summary Statement has been transmitted to the PD/PI or later than 30 calendar days after the relevant Council meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration of appeals received after the 3-week-before-Council date may be deferred to the following Council meeting. Follow both the Summary Statement rule and the Council-timing rule to ensure acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal must describe a flaw in the review process
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal letter must describe a flaw or perceived flaw in the review process for the particular application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vague complaints or disagreements about scientific judgment do not meet this requirement; the description should focus on procedural errors or process-related problems that affected the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized Organization Representative (AOR) concurrence required
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal letter must display concurrence from the authorized organization representative (AOR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters lacking AOR concurrence will not be considered formal appeals and will be treated as grievances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed basis for appeal — evidence of bias by reviewer(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: One acceptable ground for appeal is evidence of bias on the part of one or more peer reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The letter should document the alleged bias and explain how it affected the review process/outcome. Allegations of bias will be evaluated as a procedural matter, not as scientific disagreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed basis for appeal — conflict of interest (COI)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal may be based on conflict of interest (COI), as specified in regulation at 42 CFR 52h.5, on the part of one or more peer reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals involving potential COI (or violation of ethical conduct rules by NIH staff or other federal employees) will be referred to the appropriate deputy ethics counselor for consideration and resolution before any further review of, or action on, the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed basis for appeal — lack of appropriate expertise on review panel
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal may be based on a lack of appropriate expertise within the review panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appellant should explain why the panel lacked necessary expertise and how that deficiency materially affected the review of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed basis for appeal — factual errors by reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal may be based on factual error(s) made by one or more reviewers that could have substantially altered the outcome of review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the factual error(s) precisely and demonstrate how correction could have materially changed the review outcome; mere disagreement about interpretation of facts is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-eligible letters treated as grievances
rubrics_metrics.description: A letter that does not meet the formal appeal criteria and/or does not include AOR concurrence will not be considered an appeal letter but rather a grievance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grievances will not necessarily be taken to Council; they may be handled at staff level with no guaranteed further review. Ensure formal criteria are met if an appeal is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routing after study section review
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal letter submitted after study section review should be sent to the program director in NIAMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The letter will be shared with the Scientific Review Officer (SRO), who will respond in writing to the program director. Program and review staff will try to resolve issues and take appropriate action; if unresolved, the appeal and all relevant information are made available to Council for second-level review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council consideration and possible outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: If issues cannot be resolved by staff, the appeal letter and all relevant information are made available to Council. The Council may agree with either the study section or the applicant. If the Council agrees with the applicant, it recommends appropriate action to resolve the matter; if it agrees with the study section, the applicant may choose to submit a new or revised application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If re-review is recommended, the same application, not a revised or updated version, will be re-evaluated. Consult the program director for advice about options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality of Council recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council's recommendation concerning resolution of an appeal is final and will not be considered again by the NIH through this or another process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect further NIH reconsideration after Council issues its recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on contacting Council members
rubrics_metrics.description: At no time should the PD/PI or an official of the applicant organization attempt to contact individual Council members to discuss the application or appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contacting Council members could jeopardize the confidentiality and integrity of the appeals process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-review referral/assignment disputes — routing
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal of the study section or institute assignment (termed a dispute) submitted before study section review of the application should be sent to the appropriate staff in the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) or the NIAMS Scientific Review Branch if review will be by an NIAMS committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referral/review staff will respond to the letter; if the response is not satisfactory, the applicant may appeal this decision following the same process outlined for post-review appeals.
